signals.country: EU-27 (footprint: AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI)
signals.signal: AMLA's own Regulatory Instruments tracker (last updated 21/07/2026) shows the Article 28(1) AMLR Customer Due Diligence RTS still at status 'Consultation closed' - NOT 'Final report published' - as of 21/07/2026, i.e. after the 10/07/2026 statutory submission date. Same status for RTS AMLR 19(9) (business relationships / occasional & linked transactions / lower thresholds), RTS AMLR 16(4)+17(3) (group-wide requirements) and RTS AMLD 46(4) (home-host supervisory cooperation). Final reports ARE published for: RTS AMLD 53(10) pecuniary sanctions (08/07/2026), ITS AMLAR 15(3) supervisory cooperation (21/07/2026), ITS AMLR 81(1) FIU-to-EPPO, ITS AMLAR 41(2) AMLA-to-EPPO, ITS AMLD 31(2) FIU-to-FIU (03/07/2026), RTS AMLD 40(2) risk profile of obliged entities, RTS AMLAR 12(7) selection risk assessment.
signals.source_name: AMLA - Regulatory Instruments tracker (official status page)
signals.implies: The single most operationally important RTS for banks - the CDD RTS that defines exactly what identification data must be collected for standard, simplified and enhanced due diligence - is still not final with only ~11 months to AMLR application on 10/07/2027. Footprint banks (Alpha Bank, BCR, Erste, RBI, OTP, Bank of Cyprus, PrivatBank) cannot finalise eKYC/onboarding data models until it lands. Printec should pitch Namirial digital onboarding/eKYC and IMTF Siron / FICO AML as configurable, RTS-agnostic platforms - the selling argument is 'buy the engine now, configure the data fields when the RTS is adopted', not 'wait'.
signals.likelihood: Very high that CDD RTS final report + Commission delegated act land H2-2026/H1-2027; remediation projects must start regardless
signals.followup: Poll https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en monthly for the AMLR 28(1) status flip to 'Final report published'; then read the final RTS annex data-field list against Namirial/Siron field mappings.

signals.country: EU-27 (footprint: AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI)
signals.signal: AMLA published the Final Report on draft RTS under Article 53(10) AMLD6 on pecuniary sanctions, administrative measures and periodic penalty payments (press release 08/07/2026). It creates a common EU method: supervisors weigh a shared set of gravity indicators (duration, repetition, impact), classify each breach into one of FOUR levels of gravity, and apply common criteria to pick the enforcement outcome. Applies to ALL obliged sectors, financial and non-financial. Becomes directly binding in all Member States once adopted by the European Commission.
signals.source_name: AMLA press release 'AMLA introduces a common EU approach to enforcing anti-money laundering rules' + Final Report RTS Art.53(10) AMLD
signals.implies: Removes the current arbitrage where a Bulgarian or Romanian supervisor fined far less than an Austrian or German one for the same control failure. Raises the expected cost of a weak transaction-monitoring or CDD control across the whole CEE/SEE footprint, which is exactly the ROI argument for IMTF Siron AML / FICO transaction monitoring and INETCO transaction analytics upgrades. Budget trigger: banks that have deferred AML platform refresh should commit in FY2027 budgeting rounds (Sep-Nov 2026) ahead of 10/07/2027.
signals.likelihood: High - Commission adoption expected within 3-6 months of submission
signals.followup: Track the Commission Delegated Regulation adopting the Art.53(10) RTS in EUR-Lex; extract the four gravity levels to build a Printec/Siron 'fine-exposure' pitch deck per country.

signals.signal: AMLA finalised the ITS under Article 15(3) AMLAR on supervisory cooperation for direct supervision (21/07/2026). Process: national supervisors gather and quality-check the data, AMLA performs the risk assessment and makes the selection, results published on AMLA's website; full supervisory history is handed over when an entity moves to/from AMLA supervision. Direct AMLA supervision of the most significant cross-border financial institutions at GROUP level starts 2028. Follow-on: AMLA published a reporting package for identifying 'provisionally eligible' obliged entities on 12/05/2026, ran a webinar 10/06/2026, and issued an FAQ on that data collection on 22/07/2026.
signals.source_name: AMLA press release 'AMLA finalises standards for supervisory cooperation in direct supervision'; AMLA FAQ on the reporting package (22/07/2026)
signals.implies: Directly affects the footprint's cross-border groups - Erste (AT/CZ/SK/RO/HR/HU/RS), Raiffeisen Bank International (AT + 12 CEE/SEE markets), UniCredit (AT/HR/CZ/SK/SI/HU/RO/RS/BA), OTP (HU + AL/BG/HR/ME/RO/RS/SI/UA). Their CEE/SEE subsidiaries must produce group-consistent AML data on demand, in an AMLA-defined format, starting with the 2026/2027 national data collections. That is a data-quality and case-management problem, not a policy problem: sell IMTF Siron AML group-wide deployment, FICO, and a common KYC data layer across subsidiaries. Budget must commit in the FY2027 cycle (Sep 2026 - Feb 2027) to be ready for the 2027 selection round.
signals.likelihood: Certain - the data collection is already running at national level
signals.followup: Get the FAQ PDF (https://www.amla.europa.eu/document/download/0a6e81ce-e482-4de3-9941-9b6d36b004eb_en) and the reporting-package templates; map the data points to what Erste/RBI/UniCredit/OTP CEE subsidiaries can currently produce, and use gaps as the Siron/data-layer pitch.

signals.signal: EBA reporting framework release 4.3 (published 20/07/2026) contains the updated data model and XBRL taxonomy for AMLA's 2027 risk-assessment data collection on entities eligible for direct supervision. AMLA states v4.3 is for PREPARATION only and must not be used for submissions to NCAs/EBA/AMLA. A further release v4.4 is EXPECTED IN SEPTEMBER 2026, revising the templates to distinguish 'information not available' from a reported zero and adding two new data points.
signals.source_name: AMLA news 'Updated taxonomy for the 2027 risk assessment data collection'
signals.implies: A concrete, dated regulatory-reporting build for every large footprint bank: XBRL/taxonomy mapping of AML risk indicators, with a template change landing Sept-2026 and live submissions in 2027. Sells data-extraction/reporting work around AML platforms (Siron, FICO), plus the underlying KYC/transaction data quality remediation. Banks that wait for v4.4 to start scoping will miss the 2027 window - budget commit Sep-Dec 2026.
signals.likelihood: High - v4.4 explicitly scheduled September 2026
signals.followup: Watch the EBA reporting frameworks page for v4.4 in Sept-2026 and pull the two new data points; confirm the exact 2027 submission window with BNB/BNR/HNB/MNB.

signals.signal: Four AMLA consultations are OPEN with hard closing dates: draft Guidelines on ongoing monitoring of a business relationship - closes 03/09/2026 (opened 03/06/2026, public hearing held 02/07/2026); draft ITS on the format for reporting suspicions and providing transaction records (Art.69(3) AMLR) - closes 20/09/2026, public hearing 09/09/2026 10:00-12:00 CEST; draft RTS on the assessment of inherent and residual risk profile of obliged entities in the NON-FINANCIAL sector (Art.40(2) AMLD) - closes 27/09/2026; draft RTS on cross-border information exchange between FIUs (Art.31(3) AMLD) - closes 06/10/2026.
signals.source_name: AMLA - Public Consultations register
signals.implies: Two of these are direct product drivers. (a) The ongoing-monitoring Guidelines define what continuous transaction monitoring and periodic review must look like - the specification against which IMTF Siron / FICO / INETCO rulesets will be judged from 10/07/2027. (b) The Art.69(3) ITS creates a single EU suspicious-transaction-report (STR) data format with tailored data points per entity type - every footprint bank's STR interface to its national FIU (Greek HFIU, Bulgarian DANS goAML, Romanian ONPCSB, Croatian AMLO, Hungarian NAV-FIU) will need rebuilding. Printec should respond to the consultations to shape field-level requirements and, from Q4-2026, sell STR-format remediation. Budget commit: FY2027 planning, Sept-Dec 2026.
signals.likelihood: Certain (dates published by AMLA)
signals.followup: Download the Art.69(3) ITS Factsheet (https://www.amla.europa.eu/document/download/4034d0db-9eec-4f6e-8d83-ed0c44c9d46b_en) and the draft data-point model; compare with the current goAML/HFIU eSTR formats used in BG and GR.

signals.signal: NBU Board Resolution No. 81 of 15/07/2026 approved amendments to Regulation No. 65 on banks' financial monitoring (in force 17/07/2026; consolidated text now shows 'Redaktsiya vid 17.07.2026'). The amendments align Regulation 65 with Law No. 4465-IX of 03/06/2025 on financial inclusion and directly rewrite the CDD annexes: they add the e-passport / e-passport for travel abroad and the electronic taxpayer card with a QR unique electronic identifier as acceptable identification documents (Annex 2 para 9); allow a third party (accompanying or authorised person) or a bank employee to present the document where the holder cannot do so, with recorded consent (Annex 2 para 12); and replace the authorised employee's signature with a qualified electronic seal, while requiring GEOTAGGED photo capture of the customer's physical presence taken on the bank's own camera device, with photo metadata date matching the verification date and the electronic timestamp (Annex 2 para 13). [Original title: «Про затвердження Змін до Положення про здійснення банками фінансового моніторингу»]
signals.source_name: Verkhovna Rada legal database (zakon.rada.gov.ua) - NBU Board Resolution No. 81 of 15/07/2026, doc v0081500-26; consolidated Regulation No. 65 doc v0065500-20
signals.implies: A hard, in-force Ukrainian requirement that every bank branch and self-service onboarding point must capture a geotagged, timestamped photo on the BANK'S OWN device and accept e-passport/e-taxpayer-card QR credentials. That is a direct hardware+software spend: Namirial digital onboarding/eKYC with document+QR capture and geolocation metadata, camera-equipped branch kiosks/self-service units, and remote/video verification flows (Annex 3 of Reg.65 already governs videoverification). Affected: all Ukrainian banks incl. Printec reference customer PrivatBank, plus OTP Ukraine, Raiffeisen Ukraine. Budget is immediate - the rule is already in force, so this is a remediation buy, not a 2027 plan.
signals.likelihood: In force - compliance required now
signals.followup: Pull the full Annex 2/3 amended text and map the geotag/metadata and e-passport parsing requirements to Namirial capability; check with PrivatBank/OTP UA whether branch camera estate supports geolocation metadata.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) - AML enforcement
signals.signal: NBU published (07/07/2026) its June-2026 AML/CFT and FX enforcement round: measures against FOUR banks and one non-bank institution. Fines: JSC PUMB UAH 10,000,000 (breaches of CDD on new and existing customers, failure to apply enhanced due diligence to high-risk customers, failure to apply the risk-based approach / to set high risk for customers whose ultimate beneficial owners are citizens of the aggressor state, late reporting of threshold transactions to the FIU, and failure to refuse/terminate relationships where CDD documents were not provided) plus a written warning on inadequate internal AML documents; JSC UKRSIBBANK UAH 400,000; JSC TASCOMBANK UAH 200,000; JSC UNIVERSAL BANK UAH 4,096,000; LLC AI LOMBARD UAH 100,000. The preceding month (May-2026) NBU sanctioned one bank and nine non-bank financial institutions.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine - official news release on June-2026 enforcement measures
signals.implies: Monthly, named, quantified AML fines in Ukraine - the failure modes cited (CDD on existing customers, EDD on high-risk, risk-based scoring including sanctioned/aggressor-state UBOs, late threshold reporting) are exactly what IMTF Siron AML / FICO transaction monitoring and a screening+UBO data layer automate. UAH 10m against PUMB is a live, quotable ROI anchor for a Ukrainian AML pitch. Buying window is now; NBU publishes a new enforcement list every month.
signals.likelihood: High - recurring monthly enforcement cadence
signals.followup: Scrape bank.gov.ua monthly enforcement releases to build a rolling Ukrainian AML fine tracker; use PUMB/Universal Bank cases in the Siron business case.

It sits alongside a 2026 stream of ONPCSB secondary legislation: Order No. 71 of 13/05/2026 approving the Regulation on providing feedback following suspicious transaction reports received from reporting entities; Order No. 64 of 04/05/2026 on international-sanctions implementation supervision norms; Order No. 17/2026 on methodological norms for notifications and authorisation of certain funds transfers; and Government Decision No. 269/2026 repealing HG 603/2011. [Original titles in Romanian on the ONPCSB legislation page.]

signals.implies: Romanian banks (BCR - a Printec APTRA reference, BRD, Banca Transilvania, Raiffeisen RO, UniCredit RO, OTP RO) must change the technical format of their STR/threshold reports to ONPCSB again, weeks after the May-2026 feedback regulation. This also previews the bigger rebuild coming from AMLA's Art.69(3) ITS (EU-wide STR format, consultation closes 20/09/2026): Romanian banks should build the interface as configurable now rather than hard-coding Order 181.
signals.likelihood: Certain - order already issued

signals.entity: All EU Member States (footprint: AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI)
signals.signal: AMLD6 (Directive (EU) 2024/1640) has a STAGGERED transposition calendar, not a single date: Article 74 by 10/07/2025; Articles 11, 12, 13 and 15 (central beneficial-ownership registers) by 10/07/2026 - a deadline that fell three weeks ago; the bulk of the Directive by 10/07/2027, matching AMLR application; and Article 18 by 10/07/2029. The Commission had already opened infringement proceedings against 11 Member States over incomplete notification of the first (10/07/2025) tranche. [STANDING - dated 2024 for the Directive itself; the live trigger is the 10/07/2026 tranche having just passed and the 10/07/2027 main deadline now inside 12 months.]
signals.source_name: Directive (EU) 2024/1640 (AMLD6), EUR-Lex consolidated text
signals.implies: For Printec the useful read is the 10/07/2027 cliff: from that date AMLR applies DIRECTLY (no transposition) in all 10 EU footprint markets, and every obliged entity must have restructured CDD, UBO verification, EDD triggers, ongoing monitoring and STR reporting. Vendor selection for AML/KYC platforms (IMTF Siron, FICO, Namirial eKYC) has to close by roughly Q1-Q2 2027 to allow build+test, which means budget commitment in the FY2027 planning round running Sep-Dec 2026. That is the single most important selling window in this workstream.
signals.likelihood: Certain - dates fixed in the Directive/Regulation
signals.followup: Verify per-country transposition status of the Art.11-13/15 tranche in the Commission's national transposition measures (MNE) database on EUR-Lex for AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI; a country that missed it is a country whose banks are behind on UBO data.

signals.signal: At its plenary on 19/06/2026 in Paris the FATF made the initial determination that Bulgaria has substantially completed its grey-list action plan and warrants an ON-SITE assessment to verify that the AML/CFT reforms are being implemented and sustained and that political commitment remains. Bulgaria REMAINS on the FATF list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring until that on-site is completed and a subsequent plenary votes removal. Justice Minister Nikolay Naydenov represented Bulgaria. NO on-site date has been published in any source found. Bulgaria has been grey-listed since October 2023.
signals.source_name: BTA (Bulgarian News Agency) report from the FATF Paris plenary; FATF 'Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring - 19 June 2026' (FATF page Cloudflare-blocked, see access_issues)
signals.implies: Bulgaria is the first euro-area member (since 01/01/2026) still on the FATF grey list, so its banks (UniCredit Bulbank, DSK/OTP, UBB/KBC, Postbank, Fibank) currently face enhanced due diligence from correspondent banks. An on-site in H2-2026 means Bulgarian banks must demonstrate WORKING controls, not just amended law - i.e. evidenced transaction monitoring, screening, UBO verification and STR quality. That is a short-fuse, board-level buying trigger for IMTF Siron / FICO and for eKYC remediation, ahead of the on-site. Removal would then remove the EDD drag on Bulgarian correspondent relationships.
signals.likelihood: On-site likely H2-2026; removal decision plausible at the October-2026 or February-2027 plenary - NOT confirmed by any source
signals.followup: The FATF site is Cloudflare-blocked to automated fetch - an operator should open https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/High-risk-and-other-monitored-jurisdictions/increased-monitoring-june-2026.html in a browser and confirm the exact Bulgaria wording and any on-site date. Also monitor DANS (dans.bg) and strategy.bg for the accompanying ZMIP/ZMFT amendment bill.

signals.entity: European Commission / all EU obliged entities
signals.signal: Commission Delegated Regulations (EU) 2026/46 and (EU) 2026/83, adopted 03-04/12/2025 and published in the Official Journal on 09/01/2026, updated the EU list of high-risk third countries with strategic AML/CFT deficiencies; they entered into force on 29/01/2026. Bolivia and the British Virgin Islands were ADDED; Burkina Faso, Mali, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa and Tanzania were REMOVED, cutting the list from 41 to 35 jurisdictions. Listing triggers mandatory enhanced due diligence on relationships and transactions involving those countries. [STANDING - dated Jan-2026; included as the current in-force baseline, no newer delegated act found as of 02/08/2026.]
signals.source_name: EUR-Lex - Official Journal L series, 09/01/2026 (OJ L_202600083)
signals.implies: Every footprint bank's EDD country-risk table had to be repointed in Jan-2026 and will be repointed again after each FATF plenary. signals.signal: NBS adopted a NEW Decision on the conditions and manner of determining and verifying the identity of a natural person using means of electronic communication (video identification), published in Sluzbeni glasnik RS no. 43 of 08/05/2026, replacing the 2019 regime (15/2019, 84/2020, 49/2021). It requires the technical solution to deliver continuous high-quality image and sound, END-TO-END ENCRYPTION between customer and financial institution, connection to a reliable time source, and full recording of the session; NBS must be notified and the institution must evidence it meets the organisational, staffing and technical conditions before it may run video identification (NBS publishes a public list of obliged entities cleared to do so). [Original title: 'Odluka o uslovima i nacinu utvrdjivanja i provere identiteta fizickog lica koriscenjem sredstava elektronske komunikacije'] Separately, NBS amended the Decision on resident/non-resident account opening in July 2026 to tighten identification of FOREIGN natural and legal persons (in force 8 days after publication).
signals.source_name: NBS - Propisi iz oblasti sprecavanja pranja novca (AML regulations page) [NBS AML regulations register]
signals.implies: (a) Affected: every NBS-supervised bank in Serbia - Raiffeisen Serbia (a Printec x-core reference), AikBank (NCR recyclers reference), Banca Intesa, OTP Serbia, UniCredit Serbia, NLB Komercijalna. (b) What they must buy: a compliant remote-onboarding stack - Namirial digital onboarding/eKYC with E2E-encrypted video session, qualified timestamping, session recording/archive and ID-document capture; plus document management for the retained recordings, and branch/kiosk capture hardware where identification is assisted. Banks already on the 2019 rules must re-certify their solution against the new technical conditions and re-notify NBS. (c) Budget: immediate - the decision is already in force, so this is a 2026 remediation buy, and non-resident account tightening adds a second wave in H2-2026.
signals.likelihood: In force - compliance required now; NBS maintains a public list of cleared institutions
signals.followup: Pull the full text of Odluka 43/2026 from Sluzbeni glasnik and the NBS list of cleared obliged entities (https://www.nbs.rs/sr/scripts/showcontent/index.html?id=15265) to see which Serbian banks are NOT yet cleared - those are the open Namirial/eKYC opportunities.

signals.entity: Montenegro Parliament / Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG)
signals.signal: Montenegro's Parliament adopted amendments to the Law on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing which ENTERED INTO FORCE 12/05/2026. The stated purpose is full implementation of the FATF recommendations demanded by MONEYVAL and alignment with EU Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR) ahead of accession. The amendments cover governance and oversight, customer due diligence, CUSTOMER ONBOARDING, ongoing customer monitoring, and restrictions on CASH transactions. Montenegro is a non-EU footprint market mirroring the EU AML acquis in advance of AMLR's 10/07/2027 EU application date.
signals.source_name: BDK Advokati / CEE Legal Matters - 'Amendments to AML Legislation in Montenegro' (law-firm analysis; the underlying act is published in Sluzbeni list Crne Gore - gazette number not verified, see access_issues)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: all 11 Montenegrin banks - the same estate that went live on the Western Balkans TIPS clone on 20/07/2026 (CBCG, fee cap EUR 0.05 up to EUR 200), i.e. CKB/OTP, NLB Montenegro, Erste Montenegro, Hipotekarna, Lovcen, Universal Capital. (b) What they must buy: onboarding/CDD rework (Namirial eKYC), ongoing transaction monitoring aligned to AMLR concepts (IMTF Siron / FICO), and - because the amendments restrict CASH transactions - cash-handling controls and traceability at branch and ATM, which is directly Printec's cash automation/recycler (Glory, Sesami TCR, NCR) and intelligent-deposit ATM territory plus deposit-source logging. (c) Budget: now - the law is in force, and instant-payments go-live plus AML rework in the same year makes a combined self-service + AML programme the natural pitch for FY2026-27.
signals.likelihood: In force since 12/05/2026
signals.followup: Obtain the Sluzbeni list Crne Gore citation and the consolidated Montenegrin AML Act text (sluzbenilist.me) to confirm the exact cash-transaction threshold and any transition period; confirm with CBCG's banking-supervision regulations page. Cash thresholds must be verified before being quoted to a customer.

signals.country: EU-27 (footprint groups: Erste/AT, RBI/AT, UniCredit/AT-IT, OTP/HU, KBC/BE, NLB/SI, Alpha Bank/GR, Bank of Cyprus/CY)
signals.signal: AMLA's Single Programming Document 2026-2028 (published 04/02/2026) sets hard dates for direct supervision: AMLA will directly supervise 40 EU financial institutions FROM 2028; the ITS on supervisory cooperation was to be submitted to the Commission in April 2026 so that 'the first procedure for selection of obliged entities for direct supervision can begin timely in 2027 and direct supervision in 2028'; full operational readiness for the FIRST SUPERVISORY CYCLE is targeted by MID-2028; the Risk-Based Selection Framework Package (RTS under Art.12(7) AMLAR + Art.40(2) AMLD, plus a calibration note based on 2026 TESTING) must let AMLA 'enter 2027 with a tested, transparent and legally binding methodology'. By END-2027 both the selection of directly supervised entities AND the determination of supervisory FEES will be complete - and AMLA states the list of entities SUBJECT TO FEES will be LARGER than the list subject to direct supervision, with fees expected to fund ~70% of AMLA's revenue under a forthcoming Commission delegated act. Staff grows from 120 (end-2025) to 432 (end-2027). AMLA's AML/CFT Central Database rolls out in 2026 and should be FULLY OPERATIONAL in 2027, and Article 73 AMLD6 requires the Commission to transfer FIU.net management to AMLA by 10/07/2027.
signals.source_name: AMLA - Single Programming Document 2026-2028 (PDF, extracted locally with pdfminer)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: the footprint's cross-border groups. Erste (AT/CZ/SK/RO/HR/HU/RS), RBI (AT + 12 CEE/SEE markets), UniCredit (AT/HR/CZ/SK/SI/HU/RO/RS/BA), OTP (HU + AL/BG/HR/ME/RO/RS/SI/UA) are all plausible members of the 40, and a WIDER set of footprint banks will be fee-payers even if not directly supervised - i.e. they still get pulled into AMLA's data collection. (b) What they must buy: group-consistent AML data across subsidiaries feeding a supervisory data model - IMTF Siron AML group deployment, FICO, INETCO transaction analytics, and a unified KYC/UBO data layer; plus regulatory-reporting build for the AMLA Central Database and the 2027 risk-assessment collection (EBA taxonomy v4.3 now, v4.4 Sept-2026). (c) Budget: the 2026 CALIBRATION TESTING and 2027 selection mean data quality has to be fixed during 2026-2027 - budget must commit in the FY2027 round (Sep-Dec 2026), 12-18 months before the 2028 first supervisory cycle.
signals.likelihood: Very high - dates are AMLA's own published programming
signals.followup: Track the Art.12(7) AMLAR / Art.40(2) AMLD selection RTS and the Commission delegated act on AMLA supervisory fees; once the fee methodology publishes, model which footprint banks become fee-payers and use that as the door-opener conversation.

signals.signal: The Central Bank of Cyprus AML/CFT Directive K.D.P. (Regulatory Administrative Act) 120/2025 was published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Cyprus on 02/05/2025 and entered into force 02/06/2025, repealing and replacing the 5th-edition CBC AML Directive. It moves to an explicitly proportional, risk-based approach: obliged entities may tailor the FREQUENCY and SCOPE of customer reviews to each client's assessed risk level, so lower-risk customers get less frequent review. It binds all CBC-supervised obliged entities - banks, electronic money institutions, payment institutions, credit servicers, bureaux de change and financial leasing companies. [STANDING - dated 2025; the live trigger is that this Cypriot regime must now be re-tested against AMLR (Reg (EU) 2024/1624) from 10/07/2027.]
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus - Prevention and suppression of money laundering activities and financing of terrorism (official page); corroborated by Harneys and Chrysostomides law-firm notes (press)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: Bank of Cyprus (a Printec Glory TCR reference customer), Hellenic Bank, Eurobank Cyprus, Astrobank, plus the large Cypriot EMI/PI population. (b) What they must buy: risk-tiered periodic-review automation - a customer risk-scoring engine that can drive differentiated review cycles, which is exactly an IMTF Siron / FICO configuration project, plus Namirial eKYC for the re-KYC refresh workload. signals.entity: Bosnia & Herzegovina (FATF grey list) / BiH banks
signals.signal: At its plenary of 17-19/06/2026 the FATF ADDED Bosnia & Herzegovina to the list of Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring (the 'grey list'), alongside Iraq; Algeria and Namibia were removed, leaving 22 grey-listed jurisdictions. BiH made a high-level political commitment to work with FATF and MONEYVAL on an action plan with agreed timeframes. The listing follows the MONEYVAL 5th-round mutual evaluation report adopted in December 2024, which flagged fragmented governance, missing STATE-LEVEL legislation, and weak ML/TF investigations; MONEYVAL had placed BiH in ENHANCED FOLLOW-UP with a report-back due December 2026. Separately, the Pravilnik (Regulation) on implementation of the BiH AML/CFT Law was published in Sluzbeni glasnik BiH no. 8/26, implementing the Law published in Sluzbeni glasnik BiH 13/24.
signals.source_name: AML Intelligence + ComplyAdvantage + Fincrime Central reporting on the FATF June-2026 plenary (the FATF primary page https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/High-risk-and-other-monitored-jurisdictions/increased-monitoring-june-2026.html is Cloudflare-blocked to automated fetch - see access_issues/operator_requests)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: every bank in BiH - UniCredit Bank BiH, Raiffeisen Bank BiH, Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH, NLB Banka, Addiko, ASA Banka, plus the CBBH which co-launched the Western Balkans TIPS instant-payment clone on 20/07/2026. Grey-listing means correspondent banks immediately apply enhanced due diligence to BiH flows, and it lands in the same month BiH went live on cross-border instant payments - a direct clash between faster payments and slower screening. (b) What they must buy: real-time sanctions/PEP screening and transaction monitoring capable of instant-payment latency (IMTF Siron AML, FICO, INETCO transaction analytics), UBO/beneficial-ownership data remediation, and STR quality tooling to the BiH FIU; plus eKYC (Namirial) to fix onboarding CDD gaps named in the MER. (c) Budget: immediate and board-level - action-plan deadlines are agreed with FATF and the MONEYVAL enhanced-follow-up report is due December 2026, so procurement must move in H2-2026, not FY2027.
signals.likelihood: Confirmed by multiple independent reports; primary FATF text not machine-readable
signals.followup: An operator should open the FATF 'Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring - 19 June 2026' page in a browser and extract BiH's ACTION PLAN items verbatim - each action-plan line is a named control gap and therefore a named sales hook. Also get Sluzbeni glasnik BiH 8/26 for the Pravilnik's effective date.

signals.signal: At the June-2026 plenary FATF approved a PUBLIC CONSULTATION on new guidance supporting the strengthened FATF Standard on cross-border payment transparency (Recommendation 16), open to stakeholder responses from the week of 22/06/2026. The guidance is aimed at helping institutions improve payment transparency against money laundering, terrorist financing, proliferation financing and predicate crimes, with a PARTICULAR FOCUS ON FRAUD.
signals.source_name: ComplyAdvantage summary of FATF plenary June 2026 (aggregator; FATF primary page Cloudflare-blocked)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: every footprint bank sending or receiving cross-border payments, and directly convergent with the ISO 20022 structured-address mandate (SWIFT SR2026 go-live 14/11/2026, SEPA equivalent 15/11/2026, TARGET2 R2026.NOV). R.16 originator/beneficiary data quality is the AML side of the same data-quality problem. (b) What they must buy: payment-data enrichment and validation in the payment chain plus screening against structured party data - INETCO transaction monitoring, IMTF Siron screening, and integration work on the payment hub. (c) Budget: the ISO 20022 November-2026 deadline already forces this work; framing it as R.16 compliance widens the budget owner from payments to compliance.
signals.likelihood: High - consultation open, guidance expected within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Operator to retrieve the FATF R.16 consultation document from fatf-gafi.org (Cloudflare-blocked) and check whether the data-element list goes beyond the ISO 20022 structured-address minimum (Town Name + Country Code).

signals.entity: MONEYVAL / Slovenia (Urad RS za preprecevanje pranja denarja, Banka Slovenije-supervised banks)
signals.signal: MONEYVAL published Slovenia's 6th-round Mutual Evaluation Report (document MONEYVAL(2026)7) on 07/07/2026, following an on-site visit in October 2025. Based on its effectiveness and technical-compliance ratings Slovenia is placed in ENHANCED FOLLOW-UP. The report finds Slovenia has made considerable effort to understand its ML/TF risks but that the robustness of the risk assessments is constrained by structural DATA GAPS and uneven engagement across authorities, and recommends Slovenia establish a formal national AML/CFT strategic framework with measurable objectives aligned to the 2025 National Risk Assessment. [Report title: 'Anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing measures - Slovenia, Fifth/Sixth Round Mutual Evaluation Report']
signals.source_name: MONEYVAL (Council of Europe) - 6th-round Mutual Evaluation Report on Slovenia, MONEYVAL(2026)7 (rm.coe.int; Cloudflare-blocked to automated fetch - content obtained via search-engine extraction, see access_issues)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: all Banka Slovenije-supervised banks - NLB, NKBM/OTP Slovenija, SKB/OTP, UniCredit Banka Slovenija, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, Addiko - plus payment/e-money institutions. Enhanced follow-up means Slovenia must report progress to MONEYVAL on a fixed cycle, and supervisors pass that pressure straight down to obliged entities via inspections. (b) What they must buy: the named weakness is DATA - risk-assessment data quality, customer/UBO data completeness and the ability to evidence a risk-based approach. That is IMTF Siron AML / FICO risk-scoring and transaction monitoring, INETCO transaction analytics for evidencing monitoring coverage, Namirial eKYC to close onboarding CDD data gaps, and MIS/reporting to produce the data the authorities say is missing. (c) Budget: Slovenian banks should fund remediation in the FY2027 round (Sep-Dec 2026), which conveniently coincides with the AMLR 10/07/2027 programme - sell one combined AMLR + MER-remediation project rather than two.
signals.likelihood: Certain - report published and follow-up status set
signals.followup: An operator should open https://rm.coe.int/moneyval-2026-7-mer-slovenia-en/48802c71c2 in a browser and extract the Immediate Outcome ratings (esp. IO.3 supervision, IO.4 preventive measures, IO.5 legal persons/UBO) and the Recommended Actions for the financial sector verbatim - each recommended action is a named control gap and a sales hook. Also confirm which plenary adopted it (MONEYVAL 71st Plenary, 26-29/05/2026, outcome page also Cloudflare-blocked).

signals.entity: Government of North Macedonia / Financial Intelligence Unit (Uprava za finansisko razuznavanje, UFR) / NBRNM-supervised banks
signals.signal: The Government of North Macedonia adopted the 'National Strategy for Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing 2026-2029' together with its implementing Action Plan at its 152nd session on 24/02/2026; the FIU published the announcement on 06/03/2026. It follows the package of bylaws issued under the AML/CFT Law and published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of North Macedonia no. 240/2024 of 25/11/2024. [Original: 'Nacionalna strategija za borba protiv perenje pari i finansiranje na terorizam 2026-2029']
signals.source_name: Uprava za finansisko razuznavanje (FIU of North Macedonia) - official news page [FIU homepage/news]
signals.implies: (a) Affected: all NBRNM-licensed banks - Komercijalna Banka, Stopanska Banka (NBG), NLB Banka, Halkbank, ProCredit, Sparkasse - plus payment institutions and the exchange sector. North Macedonia is a non-EU footprint market aligning with the EU acquis for accession, so the 2026-2029 strategy is the vehicle through which AMLR (Reg (EU) 2024/1624) concepts land in Macedonian bank obligations ahead of the EU's own 10/07/2027 application date. (b) What they must buy: a strategy-and-action-plan cycle always converts into supervisory inspection criteria - risk-based CDD and customer risk scoring (IMTF Siron AML / FICO), remote onboarding/eKYC (Namirial), and STR reporting quality to the UFR. North Macedonia is also expected in the SECOND Western Balkans TIPS instant-payment onboarding window (November 2026), so real-time screening capability is the joint requirement. (c) Budget: FY2027 planning (Sep 2026 - Feb 2027), bundled with the TIPS-clone/instant-payments bid.
signals.likelihood: Adopted - implementation runs 2026-2029
signals.followup: Obtain the Strategy + Action Plan text from ufr.gov.mk / vlada.mk (152nd session, 24/02/2026) and extract the action-plan items addressed to REPORTING ENTITIES with their target dates - those are the datable buying triggers. Also check NBRNM (nbrm.mk) for a supervisory circular implementing the strategy.

signals.entity: European Commission (DG FISMA) vs Greece, Cyprus, Croatia, Slovakia (+ BE, DK, DE, EE, IT, PL, SE)
signals.country: EU footprint: Greece, Cyprus, Croatia, Slovakia
signals.signal: The Commission opened infringement procedures by letter of formal notice against ELEVEN Member States - Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, GREECE, Italy, CYPRUS, CROATIA, Poland, SLOVAKIA and Sweden - for failing to fully notify national measures transposing AMLD6 (Directive (EU) 2024/1640) on comprehensive access to beneficial-ownership information for legal entities, trusts and similar arrangements, whose transposition deadline was 10/07/2025. FOUR of the eleven are Printec footprint markets. The next AMLD6 tranche - Articles 11, 12, 13 and 15 on the further development of beneficial-ownership registers - fell due on 10/07/2026, and the bulk of the Directive is due 10/07/2027. [STANDING - the infringement decision dates from Sept-2025; the live trigger is the 10/07/2026 register tranche having just passed with four footprint states already in infringement on the earlier one.]
signals.source_name: European Commission infringement package 'Commission takes action to ensure complete and timely transposition of EU directives' (reported by EACCNY / FinancialCrime.lu; the Commission INF press-release page was not directly retrievable - see access_issues)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: banks in Greece (Alpha Bank - a Printec Siron AML reference, NBG, Piraeus, Eurobank), Cyprus (Bank of Cyprus - Glory TCR reference, Hellenic Bank), Croatia (Erste Croatia - OptiCash reference, ZABA/UniCredit, PBZ, OTP Croatia) and Slovakia (SLSP/Erste, VUB/Intesa, Tatra/RBI). Where the STATE has not delivered a complete, legitimate-interest-accessible UBO register, banks cannot rely on the register for verification and must carry the UBO verification burden themselves - AMLR Article 22 does not accept register data as a substitute anyway from 10/07/2027. (b) What they must buy: independent UBO/beneficial-ownership verification and corporate-structure data, screening against it, and a KYC data layer that stores and refreshes UBO evidence - IMTF Siron KYC/AML plus Namirial eKYC for corporate onboarding, and document management for the evidence trail. (c) Budget: FY2027 planning round Sep-Dec 2026, roughly 9-12 months before 10/07/2027.
signals.likelihood: High - infringement open; register tranche deadline already passed
signals.followup: Confirm the infringement package reference and current stage (LFN vs reasoned opinion) in the Commission's official infringement decisions register (ec.europa.eu/atwork/applying-eu-law/infringements-proceedings) for GR/CY/HR/SK, and check the EUR-Lex national transposition measures (NIM) list for CELEX 32024L1640 - EUR-Lex NIM returned an empty body to both WebFetch and curl this run.

signals.entity: Slovak Republic - National Council / NBS-supervised obliged entities / Financial Intelligence Unit (FSJ)
signals.signal: Act No. 73/2026 Z. z. amending and supplementing Act No. 297/2008 Z. z. on protection against money laundering and terrorist financing was ADOPTED 14/04/2026 and took effect 01/06/2026, with the provisions on the register of legal entities / beneficial-ownership data access taking effect 10/07/2026 (the same day as the AMLD6 beneficial-ownership-register tranche). Key new duties: (i) EVERY obliged entity must register in the FIU's goAML reporting system - entities that were already obliged on 01/06/2026 have until 30/11/2026, new ones within 30 days of becoming obliged; (ii) obliged persons must VERIFY beneficial-ownership information from reliable independent sources in all cases and may no longer rely solely on the register of legal entities; (iii) selected trade licences require beneficial owners to meet character requirements, with pre-31/05/2026 licence holders compliant by 30/09/2026. Reported penalty ceilings: up to EUR 1,000,000 (or double the unlawful benefit) generally and up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for banks and financial institutions. [Original: 'Zakon, ktorym sa meni a doplna zakon c. 297/2008 Z. z. o ochrane pred legalizaciou prijmov z trestnej cinnosti a o ochrane pred financovanim terorizmu']
signals.source_name: Slov-Lex - Zbierka zakonov, zakon c. 73/2026 Z. z. (primary, title/amended act confirmed); dates, goAML deadlines and penalty ceilings from KPMG Slovensko / danovky.sk analysis (press - not yet checked against the Zbierka text)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: all Slovak banks and payment/e-money institutions - Slovenska sporitelna (Erste), VUB (Intesa), Tatra banka (RBI), CSOB, Postova banka, 365.bank - plus a newly widened population of non-financial obliged entities. (b) What they must buy: a HARD 30/11/2026 goAML onboarding deadline means STR/threshold reporting interfaces must be built or rebuilt against the FIU's goAML schema this autumn - IMTF Siron reporting adapters plus integration/managed services; and the ban on relying on the legal-entities register alone forces independent UBO verification and corporate data sourcing, i.e. Siron KYC + Namirial eKYC for corporate onboarding and document management for the evidence trail. (c) Budget: IMMEDIATE - the law is already in force and the goAML deadline is 30/11/2026, so this is an H2-2026 spend, not FY2027. Note this is the same interface that AMLA's Art.69(3) STR-format ITS (consultation closes 20/09/2026) will re-cut for 10/07/2027, so sell a configurable adapter, not a hard-coded goAML build.
signals.likelihood: In force; goAML registration deadline 30/11/2026 fixed in the Act
signals.followup: Verify the 14/04/2026 adoption, 01/06/2026 / 10/07/2026 effective dates, the 30/11/2026 goAML deadline and the EUR 5m / 10%-turnover bank penalty ceiling directly in the Zbierka zakonov text of 73/2026 Z. z. before quoting them to a customer - they are currently sourced from a law/tax-firm summary. Then check the NBS AML/CFT legislation page (nbs.sk) for an accompanying supervisory opatrenie.

signals.signal: From 01/01/2026 the FMA replaced the Oesterreichische Nationalbank (OeNB) as the authority supervising and enforcing FINANCIAL SANCTIONS in the Austrian financial sector - the final step of a reform legislated in 2024. Compliance with the Sanktionengesetz for all financial-market participants (banks, payment institutions, CRYPTO-ASSET service providers, insurers) now sits with the FMA, which becomes a single one-stop supervisor for both AML/CFT and sanctions, with harmonised processes and ALIGNED INSPECTION CYCLES. Separately, FMA department head Andreas Schirk (AML/CFT and sanctions supervision) was elected unanimously by AMLA's Board of Directors as CO-CHAIR of AMLA's newly established Committee on Private Sector Standards, which develops harmonised requirements and risk indicators for financial and non-financial obliged entities. [Original titles: 'FMA ist ab 1. Janner 2026 die neue Aufsichtsbehorde zur Uberwachung und Durchsetzung von Finanzsanktionen'; 'FMA stellt Co-Vorsitzenden des Ausschusses fur Sektorstandards der EU-Geldwaschebehorde AMLA']
signals.source_name: FMA Osterreich press releases (fma.gv.at pages are Cloudflare/JS-protected to automated fetch - see access_issues; content corroborated via the APA-OTS syndication of the same release, OTS_20251230_OTS0054)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: Austrian-headquartered groups that anchor the whole Printec footprint - Erste Group, Raiffeisen Bank International, UniCredit Bank Austria, BAWAG, plus Austrian PIs/EMIs and crypto-asset service providers. Merged AML + sanctions supervision with a SINGLE aligned inspection cycle means one FMA on-site now tests screening, transaction monitoring and sanctions controls together, so a weakness in either is found in the same visit. (b) What they must buy: a unified screening and monitoring stack rather than separate sanctions and AML silos - IMTF Siron AML with sanctions/PEP screening, FICO, INETCO real-time transaction analytics, and a common list-management/data layer covering both EU restrictive measures and AML country risk. RBI in particular runs Russia-related sanctions exposure, which makes this board-level. (c) Budget: the supervisor is already live, so this is an FY2026-27 remediation buy; and because an Austrian group's controls are deployed group-wide, an Austrian win pulls through into CZ/SK/HU/RO/HR/RS/BA subsidiaries - the highest-leverage single opportunity in this workstream after AMLA itself.
signals.likelihood: In force since 01/01/2026
signals.followup: An operator should open the two fma.gv.at pages in a browser (Cloudflare-blocked to curl/WebFetch) to capture the exact statutory reference for the transfer and any FMA Rundschreiben issued in 2026 on merged AML/sanctions inspection. Track the AMLA Committee on Private Sector Standards output - an Austrian co-chair is an early-warning channel on sector-standard content.

signals.signal: On 16/03/2026 the MNB announced a formal cooperation agreement with Budapest Fovaros Kormanyhivatala, the National Tax and Customs Administration (NAV), the Supervisory Authority for Regulated Activities (SZTFH), the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of National Economy, governing Hungary's tasks towards the EU Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA). It sets the MNB's delegation of permanent and alternate representatives to AMLA's supervisory board, gives the MNB the coordination and secretariat role towards AMLA, and establishes coordinators/contact points and joint working groups. The MNB states the focus of the coming period is PREPARATION for the new AML rules, the drafting of numerous secondary and tertiary legal materials, and building methodology and tools for direct and indirect supervision, ahead of AMLA direct supervision of selected obliged entities from 2028. [Original: 'Kozosen lepnek fel a hazai felugyelo intezmenyek a penzmosas elleni nemzetkozi harcban']
signals.source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Bank - press release (2026 press releases)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: all MNB-supervised institutions - OTP Bank (a Printec footprint group across HU/AL/BG/HR/ME/RO/RS/SI/UA), K&H (KBC), Erste Hungary, Raiffeisen Hungary, UniCredit Hungary, MBH Bank. The MNB explicitly flags that it is now building supervisory METHODOLOGY AND TOOLS and further MNB rendelet-level secondary rules - i.e. a wave of Hungarian implementing regulation is coming on top of MNB Decree 14/2025 (VI.16.) on the detailed execution of AML duties and screening-system design. (b) What they must buy: screening-system design and calibration evidence (MNB Decree 14/2025 already regulates how the EU/UN restrictive-measure screening system must be developed), risk-based CDD scoring and transaction monitoring - IMTF Siron AML, FICO, INETCO - plus the data plumbing to answer MNB's new supervisory data requests. OTP as a group must make this consistent across nine footprint markets. (c) Budget: FY2027 planning round (Sep-Dec 2026), which is also when the AMLA 2027 selection data collection bites.
signals.likelihood: High - agreement signed, further MNB secondary rules explicitly announced
signals.followup: Watch mnb.hu/felugyelet/szabalyozas/penzmosas-ellen and Magyar Kozlony for the announced new MNB rendeletek and any AMLR-readiness ajanlas; pull MNB Decree 14/2025 (VI.16.) Sections on screening-system development and map them to Siron/FICO configuration.

signals.signal: The CNB published Supervisory Benchmark No. 1/2025 ('Dohledovy benchmark c. 1/2025') on 31/12/2025, setting out its methodological expectations for the VERIFICATION OF THE MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL SYSTEM IN THE AML/CFT AREA - i.e. what the CNB expects institutions' internal audit to test and evidence. The CNB's supervisory news stream also carried AMLA's 12/02/2026 launch of public consultations on three RTS (pecuniary sanctions/administrative measures, customer due diligence and identity verification, and criteria for identifying business relationships and occasional transactions), signalling that the CNB is progressively embedding AMLR methodology ahead of its mid-2027 application. Law-firm commentary reports a DRAFT NEW CZECH AML VYHLASKA in preparation; no adopted 2026 AML vyhlaska was found on the CNB site. [Original: 'Dohledovy benchmark c. 1/2025 - overovani ridiciho a kontrolniho systemu v oblasti AML/CFT']
signals.source_name: Ceska narodni banka - 'Co noveho v dohledu' (supervisory news) page
signals.implies: (a) Affected: Czech banks - Ceska sporitelna (Erste), CSOB (KBC), Komercni banka (SG), UniCredit CZ, Raiffeisenbank CZ, Moneta - plus payment institutions. A supervisory benchmark on VERIFYING the AML control system means every institution's internal audit must now produce documented evidence that monitoring rules, CDD and screening actually work, on a repeating cycle. (b) What they must buy: auditability, not just detection - model/rule tuning documentation, coverage and effectiveness reporting, and case-management audit trails from IMTF Siron AML / FICO, plus INETCO transaction analytics to evidence monitoring coverage. Institutions running spreadsheet-era AML controls fail this benchmark first. (c) Budget: the benchmark is already live, so the audit finding lands in 2026 internal-audit cycles and the remediation budget falls due in the FY2027 round (Sep-Dec 2026), conveniently merged with AMLR readiness for 10/07/2027.
signals.likelihood: In force as supervisory expectation; new AML vyhlaska draft not yet adopted
signals.followup: Download the full Dohledovy benchmark c. 1/2025 PDF from cnb.cz and extract its checklist of expected controls - it is effectively a free requirements document for a Siron/FICO gap assessment. Also monitor the Czech legislative portal (odok.cz) for the draft AML vyhlaska implementing AMLR.

signals.entity: Bulgaria - National Assembly / DANS FIU / MONEYVAL
signals.signal: MONEYVAL completed its FIFTH evaluation round of Bulgaria on 17/06/2026, rating Bulgaria 'compliant' or 'largely compliant' on ALL 40 FATF Recommendations, with R.2, 12, 18, 22, 25, 26, 27, 14, 32 and 33 upgraded from Partially Compliant. Parliament adopted the supporting legislative packages in June and July 2026, including amendments to the Criminal Code, the Criminal Procedure Code and the Administrative Violations and Penalties Act (asset confiscation, precautionary measures against bad-faith third parties, stiffer penal sanctions for LEGAL PERSONS). A FATF decision on grey-list removal is expected by END-2026, after the on-site assessment agreed at the 19/06/2026 plenary. The Measures Against Money Laundering Act (ZMIP) consolidated text published by the FSC in Feb-2026 runs only to amendments in SG No. 54/4.07.2025; secondary reporting indicates further ZMIP amendments in State Gazette (Darjaven vestnik) No. 16/10.02.2026 and No. 51/05.06.2026 - NOT verified against the gazette this run.
signals.source_name: BTA (Bulgarian News Agency) report on MONEYVAL's completion of the 5th evaluation round of Bulgaria; ZMIP consolidated English text hosted by the Financial Supervision Commission (FSC)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: UniCredit Bulbank, DSK (OTP), UBB (KBC), Postbank, Fibank, plus payment institutions - all now inside the euro area since 01/01/2026 while still grey-listed. (b) What they must buy: an FATF ON-SITE tests IMPLEMENTATION, not statute - assessors ask to see live transaction-monitoring output, EDD case files, UBO evidence and STR quality. Banks with weak evidence trails need IMTF Siron AML / FICO tuning and reporting, Namirial eKYC for CDD remediation, and INETCO transaction analytics; the euro-area/SEPA migration completed in Jan-2026 also changed transaction data formats feeding the monitoring engines, which is a concrete regression risk to close before the on-site. (c) Budget: short fuse - the on-site is expected H2-2026 and the FATF decision by end-2026, so procurement should be in-flight NOW rather than in the FY2027 round.
signals.likelihood: High - MONEYVAL 5th round closed; FATF decision signalled for end-2026 (no on-site date published)
signals.followup: An operator should retrieve the ZMIP amending acts from Darjaven vestnik (dv.parliament.bg) for SG 16/10.02.2026 and SG 51/05.06.2026 and confirm what changed for BANKS specifically - lex.bg returns a SOAP 'Unauthorized' error and strategy.bg renders only a login page to automated fetch. Also confirm the FATF on-site date; do NOT quote gazette numbers to a customer until verified.

coverage_notes: RESUMED FROM CHECKPOINT (the 02/08/2026 run was killed mid-research; the 18 signals already saved were kept unchanged and only the gaps listed in the checkpoint's 'remaining' field were researched). Gaps closed this leg: Slovenia (MONEYVAL 6th-round MER published 07/07/2026, enhanced follow-up); North Macedonia (National AML/CFT Strategy 2026-2029 adopted 24/02/2026); AMLD6 transposition/infringement status naming Greece, Cyprus, Croatia and Slovakia among 11 Member States; Slovakia (Act 73/2026 Z.z., goAML deadline 30/11/2026); Austria (FMA took over financial-sanctions supervision from OeNB 01/01/2026; FMA co-chairs AMLA's Committee on Private Sector Standards); Hungary (MNB six-authority AMLA cooperation agreement 16/03/2026); Czechia (CNB Supervisory Benchmark 1/2025 on verifying the AML/CFT control system); Bulgaria (MONEYVAL 5th round closed 17/06/2026, all 40 Recommendations C/LC, FATF decision expected end-2026). SEARCH ANGLES USED THIS LEG: English EU-level, plus local-language sweeps in Bulgarian ('Закон за мерките срещу изпирането на пари', 'Държавен вестник'), Macedonian ('Закон за спречување перење пари'), Serbian/Croatian ('Zakon o sprecavanju pranja novca', 'odluka sprjecavanje pranja novca'), Greek ('ξέπλυμα χρήματος', 'Πράξη Εκτελεστικής Επιτροπής'), Hungarian ('MNB rendelet penzmosas'), German ('FMA Geldwasche', 'Finanzsanktionen'), Czech ('AML vyhlaska CNB') and Slovak ('novela AML zakona'). Regulator news pages opened directly: ufr.gov.mk, cnb.cz, hnb.hr, mnb.hu, bankofgreece.gr, nbs.rs, bqk-kos.org, slov-lex.sk, fsc.bg. GENUINE REMAINING GAPS: (1) KOSOVO - no 2026 AML act or CBK AML regulation found; the only 2026 CBK instrument located is the 29/06/2026 Regulation on authorisation and governance of payment institutions and e-money institutions (bqk-kos.org), which references Law No. 05/L-096 on the Prevention of Money Laundering but is not itself an AML measure. Best proxy: Kosovo's AML framework remains Law 05/L-096 with FIU-K and CBK as supervisors; searched in English and Albanian-adjacent terms across bqk-kos.org, FIU-K and the Kosovo Banking Association. (2) CROATIA - no 2026 HNB Odluka or circular found on hnb.hr (the AML section's subpages last show 2024 update dates); a Croatian press portal reports a misdemeanour fine of only EUR 810 imposed on a responsible person in a credit institution for failing to analyse the background and purpose of complex/unusual transactions, notice issued 11/03/2026 - not verified against HNB and therefore NOT reported as a signal, but it is a striking illustration of the fine disparity that AMLA's Art.53(10) RTS is designed to remove. (3) GREECE - no 2026 Bank of Greece AML Executive Committee Act found; Executive Committee Act 254/1/19.01.2026 was retrieved and read but concerns payment/e-money institutions' access to payment systems, not AML.
